subject.title: [Bug]: Kimi Coding auth fallback in systemd Gateway when config env is not injected

question: Should config `env.KIMI_API_KEY` be a supported durable credential source for systemd-managed Gateway turns, or should managed Gateway runtime auth require per-agent auth profiles or service-env/SecretRef materialization?
rationale: The code can be repaired in several directions, but each changes credential persistence, status semantics, or documented setup guidance; automation should not choose that security/product contract.

options.title: Support config env for managed Gateway
options.body: Keep the documented Kimi config path valid and add service/startup/status behavior plus live proof showing systemd turns resolve the key consistently.

options.title: Prefer auth profiles for managed Gateway
options.body: Update docs and status output so managed service users are steered to per-agent auth profiles or SecretRefs instead of config env for durable provider credentials.

options.title: Clarify diagnostics only
options.body: Label config/env status as process-context scoped, accepting that runtime turns may still fail unless users move credentials manually.

recommendation.title: Support config env for managed Gateway
recommendation.body: Keep the documented Kimi config path valid and add service/startup/status behavior plus live proof showing systemd turns resolve the key consistently.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger has the strongest validated history across service-env planning and config-env behavior involved in the contract decision.
